description: Local compatibility patch carrier for the vendored Hermes gateway. Tracked in the autophagy repo, applied idempotently on deploy, reversible via backup.

patches.reason: pre_gateway_dispatch is only invoked in _handle_message; messages arriving during an active turn are queued and consumed by a recursive _run_agent continuation that never invokes the hook. This bypasses skill-generation observation (W6-4) and the meeting-gate fail-closed veto (W2-3). The patch invokes the hook exactly once at busy-entry (_handle_active_session_busy_message), guarded by an event.metadata marker; fail-safe (only an explicit skip drops).
patches.removal_condition: Remove once an upstream Hermes release invokes pre_gateway_dispatch for busy-path / queued follow-up messages (its documented 'fired once per incoming MessageEvent' contract).
patches.upstream_pr: TODO: submit upstream — pre_gateway_dispatch not fired on busy/continuation path

patches.reason: In busy_input_mode=queue, consecutive same-sender owner Discord DM text arriving during a long turn is newline-merged into ONE follow-up turn (the seam return False defers to base.py _flush_text_debounce_now -> merge_pending_message_event(merge_text=True)), mixing unrelated requests. This routes owner Discord DM text through relatedness-aware FIFO segmentation instead: UNRELATED -> separate sequential turns (arrival order in _pending_messages head + _queued_events overflow), RELATED (<=1.0s burst measured from the last physical DM, or reply-to-tail) -> merge into tail; the long task finishes uninterrupted (no interrupt/steer). Also: over-cap (>32) sends a rate-limited notice AND marks the rejected DM's receipt failed; the _MAX_INTERRUPT_DEPTH cap re-queues by prepend; each FIFO-drained follow-up turn finalizes its own per-physical-DM receipts (on_processing_complete only fires for the outer turn); and gateway start() reconciles any receipts left 'received' by a prior crash to failed. Fail-safe: any error defers to the original return False.
patches.runtime_deps: ~/.hermes/hermes-compat/hermes_compat_boot.py (flat) + ~/.hermes/hermes-compat/automation/hermes_compat/{owner_dm_relatedness,owner_dm_signal,owner_dm_dispatch,receipt_tracker,receipt_ledger,receipt_apply}.py; injected code imports via bootstrap (__path__ merge) + absolute automation.hermes_compat.*
patches.removal_condition: Remove once an upstream Hermes release segments queue-mode busy text per message (no newline-merge) with relatedness batching.
patches.upstream_pr: TODO: submit upstream — queue-mode busy text newline-merges unrelated messages

patches.reason: The 👀/✅/❌ receipt reaction attaches only to the message that STARTS a turn; merged/queued DMs get processed without any receipt. This (1) preserves ALL raw messages through the ingress text-batch merge, (2) adds 👀 at receipt to every physical owner DM, (3) resolves ✅/❌ per physical DM of the completing logical turn, with a content-free crash-visibility ledger (channel_id/message_id/state only). Fail-safe throughout.
patches.removal_condition: Remove once upstream Hermes gives a per-message receipt lifecycle for merged/queued messages.
patches.upstream_pr: TODO: submit upstream — receipt reaction is per-turn, not per-message

notes: hermes update overwrites the vendored install; re-run automation/hermes_compat/deploy.sh after any update.
healthcheck should surface a missing patch (see automation/healthcheck.sh).
This carrier does NOT hard-block gateway startup; a fail-closed ExecStartPre gate is a deliberate opt-in next step (brick risk).
